newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr races to 40-month peak, Eurobourses gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr races to 40-month peak, Eurobourses gain.

text.p: The dollar raced to fresh 40-month peaks against the mark in early trade on Tuesday, driven by U.S. figures showing strong economic growth and a growing belief that the European single currency would be turn out to be soft.

European bourses got off to a good start, despite a choppy close on Wall Street overnight which ended the market's strongest quarter in more than a decade. Paris climbed two percent to a record high after a one percent fall on Monday, with London and Frankfurt chalking up more modest gains.

The dollar hit 1.7465 marks, after 1.7432 marks at the European close on Monday, benefiting from renewed uncertainty about the strength of the euro after a big split within Germany's ruling coalition over terms of entry for the single currency.

"Once again the soft euro argument has gained the upper hand," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank, adding the dollar was also supported by fresh U.S. data on Monday signalling growth could be picking up again after several months of slowing.
Analysts also expect healthy signals on the U.S. economy to come from Tuesday's National Association of Purchasing Management survey, due a 1400 GMT, which will be good news for the dollar..

The market will be keeping a close watch on the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which starts at 1300 GMT. No announcement is seen before Wednesday but economists surveyed in a Reuters poll were unanimous in predicting no change in rates
In equities, Paris stocks surged over two percent to hit an intra-day high of 2916.57 on the CA-40 index, eclipsing the previous intra-day high of 2903.18 set last Friday.
Analysts attributed the strong rally to mainly technical reasons, following a 1.13 percent fall on Monday.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, moved ahead by 0.75 percent in thin, cautious dealings in an uncertain mood ahead of Wednesday's U.K. budget and worries over the near-term course of interest rates.
"No-one is going to be too brave before the budget tomorrow," said the head dealer at one brokerage. "It's going to be a mixed market until that's out of the way."

The rise follows a 35-point drop to 4,604.6 on Monday in the blue-chip FTSE 100 index. "It was a bad performance by the FTSE yesterday, having been up 20 points we finished through the floor," the trader said.
In Frankfurt, stocks also climbed by 0.75 percent as the stronger dollar, seen as good for exports, helped the market rebound from Monday's losses.
"There's a good potential for the market to keep up this recovery," said one Frankfurt trader, noting that the dollar was trading above 1.74 marks in European dealings.
Others said losses on Monday, tied to the overnight drop on Wall Street, did not signal a change in the market's upward trend.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 114.82 yen and 1.7464 marks, compared with 114.54 and 1.7432 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 38.7 points at 4,643.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 53.91 points to 2,912.17.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 25.91 points at 3,811.68.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $333.60 an ounce against $334.35 at Monday's close.
